title: Pork Chops with Mustard Cream Sauce
subtitle: Pan-fried pork chops with a wholegrain mustard and cream pan sauce
excerpt: Pork chops with mustard cream is a quick, weeknight pub-style dish: chops fried hard in butter until golden, then a pan sauce built in minutes from shallots, stock, cream, and wholegrain mustard. The mustard seeds give the sauce texture; the cream gives it body. It is one of the most reliable weeknight dinners in the British repertoire.

content.text: Pork chops with mustard cream sauce comes together in 20 minutes once the chops are at room temperature. The pan sauce builds from the browned residue left by the pork: shallots, stock to deglaze, cream to thicken, wholegrain mustard to finish. Do not add the mustard until the sauce is off the heat or the seeds will lose their texture.

items.prepNote: bone-in, about 200 g each, at room temperature

content.text: Season the chops generously on both sides. Heat a heavy frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the oil and {{unsalted-butter}} of butter. When the butter is foaming and nut-brown, add the chops. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes each side until deep golden. Rest on a warm plate.

In the same pan over medium heat, cook {{shallot}} chopped shallots for 3 minutes until soft. Add the thyme sprigs. Pour in {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock and scrape the browned bits from the base of the pan. Let it reduce by half.

Add {{double-cream}} of double cream. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until thick and glossy. Remove from the heat and stir in {{wholegrain-mustard}} of wholegrain mustard and {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard. Season. Remove the thyme. Return the chops to the pan, spoon over the sauce, and serve.

items.symptom: The mustard seeds have lost their texture in the sauce
items.cause: The mustard was added while the sauce was still on high heat.
items.fix: Stir in the wholegrain mustard after removing the pan from the heat. The residual warmth blooms the seeds without destroying their texture.

items.symptom: The sauce has split into greasy and watery layers
items.cause: The cream boiled too hard after the mustard was added.
items.fix: Add the cream and reduce gently. Do not return the sauce to the boil after adding the mustard.

items.cause: They went into a cold pan, or were cooked straight from the fridge.
items.fix: Always bring chops to room temperature before cooking , 20 minutes out of the fridge is enough. Use a hot pan for a sear, not a warm one.

items.symptom: The sauce tastes flat despite the mustard
items.cause: The stock was not good quality or the reduction was insufficient.
items.fix: Reduce the stock by at least half before adding cream. A concentrated stock makes a more flavourful sauce base.

content.text: Mustard cream is one of the most used pan sauce formulas in British home cooking because it works with almost any protein and takes about 10 minutes from the moment the meat comes out of the pan. With pork it is a particularly good match: the fat in the chop sweetens as it cooks and the mustard brings a sharpness that cuts through the richness without competing. Serve with mash and wilted spinach or steamed greens.
